correctness.rationale: PASS. For any color class A of size A meeting parts I, a vertex in part i has A−a_i same-colored neighbors and N−n_i total, so 2(A−a_i)>=N−n_i. A color cannot appear only within one part since degrees >0; summing over |I|>=2 gives (|I|−1)A >= (|I|N−sum_{i in I}n_i)/2 >= (|I|−1)N/2. Every used color uses at least N/2 vertices; thus no three colors. With two colors, both classes N/2, equality forces full part support and 2a_i=n_i for every part. Therefore all n_i even; conversely balanced half-splitting gives equality at each vertex. Independent half choices give prod binomial(n_i,n_i/2), color swap acts freely giving half that count. r>=2, all n_i>=1 guard all degrees positive; finite all parts.

originality.rationale: PASS, bounded best-of-knowledge. Bujtás–Dettlaff–Furmańczyk–Laskowska Observation 2(v) has the exact complete-bipartite parity case only and relates majority-C coloring to satisfactory partitions; the inspected full primary HTML does not list an arbitrary complete multipartite characterization or the class-count formula. Older satisfactory/friendly partition literature supplies balanced constructions (including Edmonds thesis Theorem 20 sufficiency for multipartite equal divisible parts) but no prior necessity for all parts, no cap of two arbitrary-color majority-C classes, or complete optimizer counts in the inspected material.
residual_risks: A differently named earlier satisfactory-partition or alliance theorem could contain the exact arbitrary-multipartite rigidity; checked primary work did not show it.
The 2015 thesis establishes half-split sufficiency, so novelty must not be attributed to this construction alone.
